package_info.package_versions: 2020.2.9 (Docker image) and Deskpro Cloud (all affected at time of report)
package_info.why_malicious: The Deskpro application contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability that allows attackers to inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of privileged users (admins and agents). This enables session hijacking, account takeover, and potentially full system compromise.

execution_context.trigger: user activity tracking (runtime, upon page visit)
execution_context.file_location: meta.pageTitle property in /portal/api/auth/session request payload (stored in database, rendered in dashboard widgets)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When an admin or agent opens the Ticket Insights dashboard, the code executes in the browser context, displaying an alert box as a proof-of-concept for XSS.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Arbitrary JavaScript execution in the browser context is a classic XSS indicator and can be leveraged for more severe attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: User-supplied data (pageTitle) should be sanitized/escaped before being rendered in the DOM. Instead, it is rendered as raw HTML/JS.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use for executing arbitrary scripts from user-controlled input in this context.
key_indicators: User input rendered unsanitized in DOM
Execution of alert() as XSS proof

execution_context.trigger: dashboard widget rendering (runtime, when admin/agent views dashboard)
execution_context.file_location: meta.pageTitle property in /portal/api/auth/session request payload (stored in database, rendered in dashboard widgets)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the dashboard is viewed, the code accesses the DESKPRO_SESSION_CODE global variable (session token) and exfiltrates it via a network request to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltration of session tokens to external domains is a clear sign of session hijacking attempts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Session tokens should never be accessible via JavaScript or exfiltrated from the browser.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use for sending session tokens to external domains.
key_indicators: Access to global session variable in DOM
Network request to external domain with sensitive data
Use of fetch/XMLHttpRequest in injected script

execution_context.trigger: dashboard widget rendering (runtime, when agent views dashboard)
execution_context.file_location: meta.pageTitle property in /portal/api/auth/session request payload (stored in database, rendered in dashboard widgets)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the agent views the dashboard, the code programmatically adds the attacker's email address to the agent's account by making an authenticated POST request using the CSRF token from the DOM.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated modification of account settings via injected scripts is a strong indicator of account takeover attempts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Email changes should require explicit user action and re-authentication, not be possible via background scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would require user interaction and confirmation dialogs.
key_indicators: Use of CSRF token from DOM in background request
Silent modification of user account data

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects malicious JavaScript payload into the pageTitle property of the meta object in a /portal/api/auth/session request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is stored in the Deskpro database and rendered in dashboard widgets.

attack_chain.action: Admin or agent opens the Ticket Insights dashboard (or any dashboard rendering the Top KB Views widget), triggering execution of the stored script in their browser context.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary JavaScript executes in the victim's browser.

attack_chain.action: Malicious script exfiltrates session token (admin session hijack) or modifies account settings (agent account takeover).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains admin/agent privileges, can perform privileged actions, and potentially lock out legitimate users.

behavioral_signatures: User-supplied data rendered unsanitized in DOM
Execution of script tags from database-stored fields
Network requests to external domains containing session tokens or sensitive data
Silent modification of user account data via background JavaScript
file_indicators: meta.pageTitle property in /portal/api/auth/session payload containing <script> tags
Dashboard widgets rendering unsanitized user input
network_indicators: Outbound requests to untrusted/external domains from Deskpro admin/agent dashboard context
Requests containing session tokens or CSRF tokens in query/body
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for script tags or suspicious JavaScript in user-controlled fields (e.g., pageTitle). Inspect dashboard rendering logic for unsanitized data insertion. Detect outbound network requests from the Deskpro admin/agent dashboard to external domains, especially those containing session or CSRF tokens. Alert on background requests that modify user account data without user interaction.
